explication:
<explanation>
1. Identify the project type and purpose  
   - This is an open-source Claude Code plugin (“n8n-skills”) that supplies seven distinct AI “skills” for building and validating n8n workflows via the n8n-mcp server.  
   - Its goal is to teach Claude-powered AI agents best practices for expression syntax, tool usage, workflow patterns, validation, node configuration, and code nodes (JavaScript/Python) when constructing automation in n8n.

2. Analyze the file structure  
   Top-level directories and files:
   • .claude-plugin/             → Plugin manifest (plugin.json, marketplace.json)  
   • dist/                       → Packaged ZIPs (ready for marketplace or manual install)  
   • docs/                       → Development, installation, usage, testing guides  
   • evaluations/                → JSON files defining test scenarios per skill  
   • skills/                     → Seven folders, one per skill (each with SKILL.md and supporting docs)  
   • .mcp.json.example           → Example config for n8n-mcp server  
   • README.md, CLAUDE.md        → High-level overview and Claude-specific instructions  

   Observations:
   - Modular structure: each skill is a self-contained unit.  
   - Build/deployment pipeline: source → dist ZIPs.  
   - Test harness: evaluation JSONs map to automated or manual quality-assurance runs.  
   - Configuration: plugin.json and marketplace.json define metadata for Claude Code plugin system.  

3. Examine the README for additional insights  
   - Lists the seven skills and activation triggers.  
   - Emphasizes event-driven activation: skills “activate when relevant queries are detected.”  
   - External dependencies: n8n-mcp server, Claude API/Claude Code CLI.  
   - Testing: “claude-code --skill …” or npm test.  

4. How to create an accurate system design diagram  
   a. Identify main components  
     • Claude Code Plugin Loader  
     • Skill Modules (7 folders under /skills)  
     • Evaluation/Test Harness (JSON scenarios under /evaluations)  
     • Documentation Site (docs/)  
     • Distribution Pipeline (scripts/zipping into dist/)  
     • External Services:  
       – n8n-mcp MCP Server (API endpoint)  
       – Claude API / Claude Code CLI  

   b. Determine relationships and interactions  
     1. Plugin Loader reads plugin.json → registers each skill.  
     2. User query enters Claude Code CLI or Claude.ai → Plugin Loader invokes matching skill module.  
     3. Skill module logic may:  
        – Query n8n-mcp server (via REST API) for node lists, templates, validations  
        – Perform internal guidance (patterns, code snippets)  
     4. Evaluation harness feeds sample inputs → verifies skill outputs against evaluations/*.json.  
     5. On release: source is packaged as ZIPs in dist/ → published to marketplace or installed manually.  

   c. Highlight architectural patterns and design principles  
     • Plugin/extension framework: Declarative metadata + runtime discovery  
     • Event-driven activation: Skills trigger on keyword patterns  
     • Modular and layered:  
       – Skill layer (business logic guidance)  
       – Test layer (evaluations)  
       – Packaging layer (dist)  
       – Documentation layer (docs)  
     • Separation of concerns: Each skill folder contains its README, SKILL.md, pattern docs, examples.  

   d. Relevant technologies and frameworks  
     • JSON manifests: plugin.json, marketplace.json, evaluation definitions  
     • ZIP packaging for distribution  
     • Node-style module layout (although code is largely content/config)  
     • CLI integration: claude-code commands  
     • REST API calls to n8n-mcp server  

5. Tailoring the diagram for an open-source tool  
   - Emphasize core functionality: the seven Skill Modules and how they register/activate  
   - Show extensibility: adding a new skill is as simple as creating a new folder under /skills with a SKILL.md and metadata  
   - Illustrate integration with other systems: Claude Code environment and n8n-mcp server  

6. Diagram drawing guidelines  
   - Use clear labels for each box: e.g., “Plugin Loader”, “Skill: n8n-Expression-Syntax”, “n8n-mcp Server”  
   - Draw directional arrows:  
     → from “User Query” to “Plugin Loader”  
     → from “Plugin Loader” to individual Skill Modules  
     → from Skill Modules to “n8n-mcp Server”  
     → from “Skill Modules” to “Evaluation Harness” (for testing)  
   - Color code / shape code:  
     • Plugin core (blue rectangles)  
     • Skill modules (green rounded boxes)  
     • External services (orange cylinders or cloud shapes)  
     • Testing harness (gray dashed box)  
   - Annotate connections with protocols or data types: e.g., “HTTP/JSON” for n8n-mcp calls, “CLI” for user input.  

7. Key emphasis  
   - Capture every layer (source, test, docs, dist, runtime)  
   - Show data/control flow from user input to skill activation, to external calls, back to user output  
   - Keep it modular—each skill is a distinct component that plugs into the core loader  
   - Do not oversimplify by lumping skills together; represent each major group or pattern  

By following these steps, the principal engineer can draft a comprehensive architecture diagram that highlights the modular plugin framework, skill activations, test integration, packaging pipeline, and external service dependencies that make up the n8n-skills project.
</explanation>
